correctness.rationale: The exact full matching probability follows by a bijection between each eligible exceptional-agent priority position and the unique compatible ordering of common agents. The sum of common-agent object indices proves the Pareto iff suffix record equivalence without relying on finite samples. Suffix maxima give a monotone step-function composition, with an explicit preference ranking realizing every composition. Sequential conditional uniform ranks give its profile-frequency formula; independent right-to-left record ranks give the Stirling generating function and moments. Boundaries \(n\ge2\), all/identical/reverse exceptional rankings, and uniform priorities are explicit. Direct independent exact integer/fraction calculations passed 872 full profiles for \(2\le n\le6\), 1,077,736 priority outcomes, 495,781 positive matching checks, 15,016 exhaustive Pareto tests, and 64 ordered-composition types at \(n=7\); finite corroboration is not promoted to an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Checked full primary texts show that the two-type marginal-probability algorithm, RSD axiomatic characterizations, and small fixed-market support censuses do not imply the general joint matching probability \(t_x/n!\), all compositions, and Stirling-profile distribution. A same-object two-preference-type algorithm is explicitly credited. Searches are not uniqueness proof; inaccessible near-common and tiered-domain full texts leave priority uncertainty.
residual_risks: Full primary article by Chang and Chun (2017) on near-common rankings was inaccessible; accessible abstract and Brandt et al. domain definition suggest different model and questions, but full-text overlap remains unexcluded.
A tiered-domain 2023 RSD paper was available only in abstract; specialized probability results in the text are unknown.
An independently rediscovered suffix-record/composition formula might appear unindexed or in different probability/combinatorics terminology; literature search is not a novelty certificate.
Fixed-size small-market support tables overlap special cases; only the all-n, all-composition classification and profile-frequency law are claimed as distinct.

value.rationale: One exceptional preference is a canonical structural departure from unanimity in one-sided matching. The exact joint allocation lottery captures correlations not present in agent-object marginals, compresses factorial outcome uncertainty into \(n\) suffix counts, and gives natural all-n support/shape distributions with all compositions and unsigned Stirling frequencies; these are structurally motivated complete classifications rather than a routine finite subcase.
